draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Sulthan Bathery! The name comes from Tipu Sultan's army, which used a 13th-century Ganapathi Temple here to store ammunition. British records turned "Sultan's Battery" into Sultan Bathery.
draft.hungryLine: Bathery is the busiest commercial town in Wayanad, so you won't go hungry. Wander the town centre and eat where the locals queue.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at the old Ganapathi Temple, the one Tipu's army used as its battery, then walk the busy town centre.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Slow down with a tea in town and watch Wayanad's busiest market go by.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Before it was Tipu's battery, this was Kidanganad village, named after the Kidangan tribe who lived here.

tips.title: Carry a rain layer.
tips.body: Kerala gets rain for at least seven to eight months a year.

tips.title: Onam is in Aug or Sep.
tips.body: Kerala's biggest festival falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam, and shops run big discounts.

story.title: The land of swamps
story.body: Emperor Erayappa of the Ganga dynasty conquered this region and called it Bayalnad, the land of swamps.

story.title: Brothers at war
story.body: Erayappa's sons Rachamalla and Battunga fought over the kingdom. Rachamalla was killed and Battunga ruled Bayalnad.

story.title: A temple is built
story.body: A Ganapathi Temple was built in what was then Kidanganad village, named after the Kidangan tribe.

story.title: Sultan's Battery
story.body: When Tipu Sultan of Mysore invaded Malabar, his army used the old temple to store ammunition. British records later wrote the name as Sultan Bathery.

story.title: Wayanad's market town
story.body: Sulthan Bathery is the taluk headquarters and the most commercially active town in Wayanad district.
